quotes.text: Integrate Link using the Payment Element or Contact Details Element.
You must capture an authorized Link payment within 7 days of the authorization. Otherwise, the authorization is automatically canceled and you can’t capture that payment.
Configure your integration to listen for these events rather than waiting on a callback from the client.
To accomplish this, create a `CustomerSession` on the server and return its `client_secret` as `customerSessionClientSecret` to the front end.

old_evidence.text: Integrate Link using the Payment Element or Link Authentication Element.

To accomplish this, create an Ephemeral Key and send it to your front end along with the `Account` ID (for customers represented as customer-configured `Account` objects) or the `Customer` ID (for customers represented as `Customer` objects).

findings: Both captures describe custom Web Elements checkout using a server-created PaymentIntent and a client Elements group initialized with its scoped client secret. Dashboard Link enablement and omitting payment_method_types apply to dynamic methods. Publishable-key browser initialization, direct Stripe.js hosting in HTML, and HTTPS for live acceptance are documented (old raw lines 19-54, 166-168 and 234-252, new raw lines 20-62, 173-175 and 243-261).

Email options remain prefill a known email into the Payment Element, collect it directly there, or use a separate email/authentication Element with the optional shipping Address Element before Payment Element. The first route has no shipping collection. The separate component may be shown once on an earlier page. An existing Link account match triggers a phone code and successful authentication enables saved-address/payment autofill. A supported payment method is a qualification for the non-enrolled Payment Element prompt. Prefill starts authentication and the change callback reads event.value.email (old raw lines 119-164 and 409-620, new raw lines 107-170 and 416-617).

Both captures call the React shipping component ShippingAddressElement in setup prose (old raw lines 425-427 and new raw lines 432-434). In each React shipping example, the PaymentIntent flow instead imports AddressElement from the root @stripe/react-stripe-js package and sets mode: 'shipping' (old raw lines 795-833 and new raw lines 790-825). This mismatch is inherited from the May capture.

Client stripe.confirmPayment receives the shared Elements group and a return URL. Intermediate authorization and redirect configuration can affect browser navigation. Return parameters identify the PaymentIntent and client secret for status lookup, while server webhooks drive fulfillment after payment_intent.succeeded and support failure handling. Separate manual authorization reaches requires_capture, with cancel or capture within seven days and no capture above the authorized amount (old raw lines 966-1127, new raw lines 954-1101). The existing summary lines 46-56 retain the seven-day limit and return parameters but omit these state and fulfillment boundaries.

CustomerSession redisplay and durable Link instrument reuse are separate operations. Redisplay uses the same customer_account for a customer-configured Account or customer for a Customer on both server resources, enables Payment Element redisplay, and passes separate CustomerSession and PaymentIntent client secrets. Reuse is for future off-session payments or subscriptions and excludes future on-session use in this guide. The examples set setup_future_usage=off_session then confirm another PaymentIntent with the matching customer identity and resulting PaymentMethod ID (old raw lines 1162-1412, new raw lines 1136-1332). Both captures say confirmation with off_session=true returns an error when authentication is required while the customer is absent (old raw lines 1368-1370, new raw lines 1300-1302). The current source lines 11-56 omit both topics.

The existing source lines 17-21 describe the separate component only as a shipping choice and omit Address Element optionality for a single email/auth field without shipping. Both captures explicitly support that separate-component use (old raw lines 149-158 and new raw lines 147-156). The collect-in-Payment-Element summary row's no-shipping condition also merits wording as an integration selection cue since the direct email-collection passage describes the Link email interaction and the separate documented shipping flow rather than a general platform prohibition (old raw lines 141-158 and new raw lines 139-156).

Sandbox OTP results and 3DS2 examples describe simulation and the snapshots warn against storing real user data in sandbox Link accounts. The guide assigns disclosure and consent responsibilities for Stripe's Elements data collection (old raw lines 1129-1160 and 1414-1416, new raw lines 1103-1134 and 1334-1336).
substantive_changes: The separate-component path now uses Contact Details Element, React ContactDetailsElement and Stripe.js contactDetails for setup and shipping, in place of the old Link Authentication Element, LinkAuthenticationElement and linkAuthentication. The overall order and email/authentication behavior largely align across versions. This is an integration surface change, including prefill, change handler and shipping examples (old raw lines 149-158, 409-620 and 785-926, new raw lines 147-156, 416-617 and 780-914).

Saved-method display changes from Ephemeral Key with customerOptions and elements_customers_beta_1, including the old 2026-04-22.dahlia API version examples, to a server-created CustomerSession with redisplay enabled and separate customerSessionClientSecret. The matching Accounts v2 and Customers v1 identity variants are retained. Connect availability vs other-user public preview and preview-version requirement remain; the new capture adds the Dashboard Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts opt-in instruction (old raw lines 1162-1312 and 1318-1324, new raw lines 1136-1256 and 1262-1268).

Both captures' general dynamic-method guidance pairs Dashboard Link enablement with omission of payment_method_types (old raw lines 37-46, new raw lines 45-54). The older prose separately called automatic_payment_methods optional and gave manual-listing advice for a future-use Setup Intents case, which the new section routes to another guide. Manual-capture and both redisplay PaymentIntent examples replace explicit payment_method_types: ['link', 'card'] with automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true (old raw lines 1082-1093, 1181-1208 and 1212-1239, new raw lines 1063-1074 and 1151-1191). Future reuse examples already enabled automatic methods in both captures (old raw lines 1326-1412, new raw lines 1270-1332). The example changes are scoped to their requests.

The hosted HTML example moves from Dahlia to Endive while direct loading remains. The old test section expressly included domain registration and said only credit/debit cards and qualified US bank purchases worked; the new text lists these as supported and omits registration. Additional-funding wording changes from same settlement time and guarantees to same settlement time and processing behavior. These differences qualify what can be repeated as current guidance (old raw lines 234-247 and 1129-1148, new raw lines 243-256 and 1103-1122).

Node/Express versus Ruby/ERB setup, SDK versus curl formatting for unchanged operations, updated image URLs and textual workflow diagrams, heading/table/code formatting, TypeScript fence correction, and See also routing are presentation, examples or navigation. The new CLI sandbox note is documentation for agents and sandbox provisioning, separate from the merchant account onboarding and payment flow (old raw lines 19-117 and 1418-1424, new raw lines 20-105 and 1338-1344).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/add-link-elements-integration, the November guide documents custom web Elements checkout backed by a server-created PaymentIntent. For dynamic methods it enables Link in Dashboard and omits payment_method_types, passes the PaymentIntent client secret to browser Elements, and requires HTTPS for live use. It prefers passing known email to the Payment Element, supports collecting it directly there, and uses Contact Details Element before the optional shipping Address Element and Payment Element for a combined email and Link authentication path. An existing Link account match prompts a phone code, with saved details available following successful authentication. The email paths preserve the core May flow while changing the separate Element used by setup and shipping. The mapped source-stripe-add-link-elements-integration.md summarizes May's Link Authentication Element, prefill, shipping, capture and redirect. Client confirmPayment and return parameters provide a status lookup path, webhooks drive fulfillment after payment_intent.succeeded, and a manually authorized PaymentIntent reaches requires_capture with the seven-day Link deadline. Optional server CustomerSession redisplay uses a separate client secret and consistent customer_account or customer identity, while future off-session or subscription reuse attaches the PaymentMethod to that identity. Later confirmation uses a new PaymentIntent with the matching customer and resulting PaymentMethod IDs. Both captures say confirmation with off_session=true returns an error if authentication is required while the customer is absent. See old raw lines 32-50, old raw lines 119-168, old raw lines 966-1127, old raw lines 1162-1312 and old raw lines 1368-1370, alongside new raw lines 40-62, new raw lines 107-175, new raw lines 954-1101, new raw lines 1136-1256 and new raw lines 1258-1332, especially new raw lines 1300-1302.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/add-link-elements-integration, the substantive changes missing from source-stripe-add-link-elements-integration.md are ContactDetailsElement/contactDetails for setup and shipping and CustomerSession redisplay with its separate customerSessionClientSecret. The capture also adds Dashboard opt-in instructions, with Accounts v2 generally available to Connect users and in public preview with preview versioning for other Stripe users. The browser example script moves from Dahlia to Endive. Keep the older Link Authentication Element/linkAuthentication, Ephemeral Key/customerOptions beta, 2026-04-22.dahlia examples, domain-registration line and funding wording dated to May 8, 2026. The registration index still lists Link and routes to Dashboard/API variants. Both captures direct dynamic-method adopters to turn on Link in Dashboard and omit payment_method_types. May separately called automatic_payment_methods optional and gave Setup Intents manual-listing advice, while November links to the future-payments guide. The manual-capture and both redisplay PaymentIntent examples replace explicit link/card lists with automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true. The future-reuse PaymentIntent examples enable automatic methods in both captures. Those examples establish their shown request configurations. Ruby/ERB instead of Node/Express, curl for otherwise matching operations, diagrams, image paths, table formatting and See also routes are presentation or navigation. Carry separate reciprocal warnings for the November React confirmation example that still renders LinkAuthenticationElement and the redisplay snippet that imports it, and for the inherited React shipping mismatch. Both captures' prose calls it ShippingAddressElement, but the PaymentIntent shipping examples use the root @stripe/react-stripe-js AddressElement in shipping mode. ShippingAddressElement belongs to the distinct Checkout Sessions React path documented in the Address Element concept. Keep the PaymentIntent and CustomerSession client secrets, browser status lookup, authorization, capture and server fulfillment distinct. Link method reuse is scoped to off-session payments or subscriptions and sandbox examples simulate outcomes.
